marketSizing.description: Market sizing frameworks help estimate the revenue opportunity for a business. The TAM-SAM-SOM approach narrows from total market to addressable opportunity.

approaches.name: TAM (Total Addressable Market)
approaches.description: The total market demand for a product or service, assuming 100% market share with no competition. Represents the maximum revenue opportunity.
calculationMethods: Top-down: Start with industry reports, narrow by geography and segment
Bottom-up: Number of potential customers × average revenue per customer
Value theory: How much value does your solution create for the market?

approaches.name: SAM (Serviceable Addressable Market)
approaches.description: The segment of TAM targeted by your products/services that is within your geographic reach and fits your business model.
calculationMethods: TAM filtered by: geography, customer type, pricing tier, distribution capability
Focus on segments you can actually reach with your current business model

approaches.name: SOM (Serviceable Obtainable Market)
approaches.description: The portion of SAM that you can realistically capture in the near term (1-3 years), considering competition and resources.
calculationMethods: SAM × realistic market share (typically 1-5% for startups in year 1)
Bottom-up from sales capacity, marketing budget, and conversion rates
Comparable company analysis: what share did similar companies achieve?

competitiveAnalysis.description: Frameworks for understanding the competitive landscape and positioning your business.

templates.name: Competitive Matrix
templates.description: Compare competitors across key dimensions relevant to customer decisions
templates.usage: Plot competitors on a 2×2 matrix using the two most differentiating dimensions

templates.name: Strategic Group Analysis
templates.description: Identify clusters of competitors with similar strategies
templates.usage: Group competitors by strategic similarity to find gaps and opportunities

templates.name: Blue Ocean Strategy
templates.description: Create uncontested market space by simultaneously pursuing differentiation and low cost
principles: Eliminate: Which factors the industry takes for granted should be eliminated?
Reduce: Which factors should be reduced well below the industry standard?
Raise: Which factors should be raised well above the industry standard?
Create: Which factors should be created that the industry has never offered?

customerSegmentArchetypes.description: Common customer segment patterns that appear across industries

archetypes.name: Early Adopters
archetypes.description: Tech-savvy, risk-tolerant customers who try new products first
characteristics: Willing to pay premium for novelty
archetypes.reachStrategy: Product communities, tech blogs, beta programs, influencer partnerships

archetypes.name: Price-Sensitive Pragmatists
archetypes.reachStrategy: Price comparison sites, referral programs, free trials, money-back guarantees

archetypes.name: Conscious Consumers
archetypes.description: Customers who factor social and environmental impact into purchasing decisions
characteristics: Willing to pay 10-25% premium for sustainability
High brand loyalty when values align
archetypes.reachStrategy: Sustainability certifications, impact reports, purpose-driven content, community engagement

archetypes.name: Enterprise/B2B Buyers
archetypes.description: Organizational buyers with formal procurement processes
archetypes.reachStrategy: Account-based marketing, case studies, demos, procurement compliance, ESG reporting

archetypes.name: Underserved/BOP Markets
archetypes.description: Base-of-pyramid markets with significant unmet needs
archetypes.reachStrategy: Mobile distribution, agent networks, microfinance partnerships, community trust-building

financialPlanning.description: Key financial planning frameworks for business plans

elements.name: Unit Economics
elements.description: Revenue and costs associated with a single unit of your business model
elements.importance: Validates whether the business model is fundamentally viable before scaling

elements.name: Break-even Analysis
elements.description: The point at which total revenue equals total costs
elements.formula: Break-even units = Fixed Costs / (Price per unit - Variable cost per unit)
